answer.summary: Mullenweg warned that businesses on proprietary platforms such as Facebook or Shopify can succeed, then have access or APIs changed—or be pressured to give up ownership or be shut off. He said open source offers more lasting freedom because people retain the ability to use, fork, own, and build on the code.

sections.heading: Risk of building on proprietary platforms
sections.content: His example was companies building on platforms such as Facebook or Shopify, becoming successful, and then having the platform pull the rug out from under them by changing an API or removing access. He described platform owners demanding warrants and a stake in a company, or threatening to shut its app off.

sections.heading: What offers lasting freedom
sections.content: Mullenweg said, “you don't have freedom unless you're building on open source.” As an example, he said that even if WordPress’s leadership became hostile, WordPress would still belong to users as well: people could fork the code, own it, and continue building on it.
